findings: Cold review of both conclusions against the revised corpus (F-4 = the 239 count alone, F-6 = the dominance ratio 239:43). All four ledger commands were re-run against docs/fixtures/research-v2-live-escalated.ledger.jsonl and reproduce exactly: contest.gate=26, survey.gate=6, total regression-item=239, checklist:regression=43:239. C-1 (DERIVED): answers A-1 and cites F-2/F-3. A-1 demands the per-fire count at the densest gate be MEASURED not estimated; F-2 supplies exactly that (26 at contest.gate, kind=command, from a real ledger) and F-3 supplies the depth-dependence (6 at survey.gate), so 'not a small constant, rises with depth' follows directly from the two cited findings. Diagnostic-wise F-2/F-3 are marked inconsistent with H-1 and H-3 in contest.json, consistent with H-2 -- the per-fire depth-growth is what kills the 'bounded per-fire' clause both H-1 and H-3 share. C-1 (CALIBRATED): starting_level=high, one downgrade (imprecision: single dense ledger, counts vary with density/retries) -> high minus one step = moderate. Arithmetic correct and the judgment is honest: it rests on ONE ledger, and 'moderate' does not overclaim generality. APPROVE. C-2 (DERIVED): answers A-2, cites F-1..F-6, hypothesis H-2. A-2 asks linear vs superlinear decided from recorded counts. The load-bearing claim is the code mechanism F-1/F-5 (credibility 3, file source S-4): the loop re-runs EVERY earlier control UNCONDITIONALLY (full cumulative history, no keep-best/pass-only filter). Given that mechanism, aggregate work = sum over gates of prior-control count = a triangular sum = superlinear/quadratic in the number of gates -- a structural derivation, not a two-point extrapolation. The per-gate point measurements (6->26) corroborate the rising slope but are not the sole basis. This is the correct reading of the CALIBRATED probe: the quadratic claim is NOT overreach because it is anchored on the unconditional-re-run code (cred-3 evidence) with the point counts as corroboration, and the conclusion explicitly downgrades on 'indirectness' (the total is derived, not read off one recorded total-work metric) and names the exact falsifier that would break it (gate code filtering the regression set to keep-best/current-macro, which would collapse the triangular sum to linear). Refutation check against contest.json: H-1 (bounded per-fire AND linear total) is scored inconsistent by all six findings -> refuted; H-2 (quadratic total) consistent by all six -> survives; H-3 (bounded per-fire, quadratic total) is scored inconsistent by F-1/F-2/F-3 on its per-fire-bounded clause while consistent only on F-4/F-5/F-6 -> refuted via the per-fire diagnostics. So 'H-1 and H-3 refuted, H-2 survives' is fully supported by the ACH matrix, and the distinguishing evidence between the two survivors-in-aggregate (H-2 vs H-3) is exactly the per-fire depth-growth of F-1/F-2/F-3. F-6 (239 vs 43, ~85% of grading) substantiates '239 regression verdicts dominate all grading'. C-2 (CALIBRATED): starting_level=high, one downgrade (indirectness) -> moderate. Arithmetic correct; 'moderate' is honest given the aggregate is inferred rather than directly logged. One residual caveat worth noting (not a defect): strict quadratic assumes controls-added-per-gate does not decay; if it did, growth would be sub-quadratic but STILL superlinear, and the answer A-2 needs only superlinear, which the unconditional-re-run mechanism robustly establishes -- so hedging to 'superlinearly (quadratically)' with a moderate label is appropriately calibrated, not an overclaim. Both conclusions derive from their cited findings, both calibrations pass the high-minus-one-downgrade=moderate arithmetic and the honesty test, and the refutation is backed by the contest matrix. APPROVE.
